hero.heading: Shred A Billion Wiki: Where to Play and How to Start
hero.lead: Play [Shred A Billion on Roblox](https://www.roblox.com/games/125332227026284) from the official game page. Look for Blue Chip studios as the creator so you know you’re opening the Roblox game covered here. In the bank vault, you start with a hand vac and earn coins by running bundles of bills through the shredder. You can bring up to three friends, and digging deeper gives you a new goal: finding the key to the gold vault. The table and steps below show what to look for on Roblox, how to get started, and what to aim for after your first batch of coins.

sections.heading: Start With the Hand Vac and Shred Cash for Coins
sections.intro: Your first tool is a small hand vac. Use it to collect bills in the bank vault, then take the cash to the shredder. The bills are what you gather; coins are what you earn when you shred the collected cash. Keeping those two stages distinct makes the first progression goal clear: collect bundles, process them, and use the resulting coins to work toward better equipment.
paragraphs: The listed equipment progression includes backpack vacs, the Mega Vac, and the Black Hole. These are goals to work toward as you shred more cash, but their exact prices and unlock requirements are not established here. Check the in-game equipment options as you earn coins so you can see which purchase is currently available rather than planning around an assumed cost.

For an early run, focus on moving cash through the full sequence: collect bills with the hand vac, bring them to the shredder, and confirm that shredding has added coins before choosing an upgrade. Collecting a large amount of cash does not itself mean those bundles have already become spendable coins; they need to be shredded first. Once you can access a stronger vacuum, the same collect-and-shred sequence remains the basis of your progress. The beginner guide covers first steps, while the tools guide focuses on equipment.

sections.heading: Watch for Monsters After Dark
sections.intro: Monsters appear at night in Shred A Billion. Before you head farther in, decide what you want to finish on this trip. If you’re close to completing what you came to do, you can wrap it up and leave the next stretch of digging for another trip.
paragraphs: If you’d rather keep digging after dark, pick a stopping point before you go farther, such as the end of the section you’re already working on. That gives you a clear point to turn back instead of letting one more stretch turn into a much longer trip.

sections.heading: Bring Friends and Find the Roblox Group Bonus
sections.intro: The Shred A Billion listing on Roblox advertises 100 coins for joining the group. If you want the bonus, join with the Roblox account you use to play, then check your in-game coin balance before counting on those coins for an upgrade.
paragraphs: The Shred A Billion listing on Roblox advertises 100 coins for joining the group. If you want the bonus, join with the Roblox account you use to play, then check your in-game coin balance before counting on those coins for an upgrade.
bullets: Count yourself when planning a co-op session. You can bring up to three friends, for four players total.
Look for the group offer in the game description on Roblox. The advertised reward is tied to joining that group.

faq.question: How do I move gold to the hideout?
faq.answer: Once the gold vault is open, load the gold onto a cart and ride it back to the hideout. The destination is different from the one you used for bills: ordinary cash goes to the shredder, while the gold goes to the hideout.

faq.question: What does the heist leaderboard track?
faq.answer: It ranks heists by how quickly they’re completed. If you want to see how your run compares with others, look at the time for the gold heist rather than the coins you earned shredding cash earlier. The leaderboard is for the fastest heists, not for money collected.

faq.question: How many friends can I play with?
faq.answer: You can bring three friends, which makes four players including you. If you’re organizing a session, count the three as guests, not as the total group size. If four friends want to join you, you’ll need to split the group or take turns.
